laws.rule: Florence's urban police regulation bans lying on public ground or on the steps of monuments, churches and memorials, and camping out, eating, drinking or sleeping there in a plainly indecent way or by taking over public space with bags or equipment. The general fine for breaching the regulation is EUR 80 to EUR 500 (about A$127 to about A$795, RBA rate of 30 October 2026).

laws.rule: Tuscan-Emilian Apennine National Park: camping is prohibited outside equipped areas. In park zones 2 and 3, bivouac with a tent is allowed from sunset to sunrise; check the park map for the relevant zone.
Foreste Casentinesi National Park: the park says dogs must be kept on a lead and comply with veterinary requirements. Check local trail conditions and any more specific restrictions before walking.
In Tuscany, non-residents must obtain a tourist authorisation before collecting wild mushrooms. Municipal restrictions and separate park rules can also apply; check the area before collecting.
laws.heading: Toscana: raccolta funghi, disposizioni

laws.rule: Tuscany allows mushroom collecting from one hour before sunrise to one hour after sunset. The region requires rigid, ventilated containers and prohibits plastic bags and tools that damage the forest floor.

laws.rule: Siena's Police Regulation (Regolamento di Polizia Urbana, council resolution 146 of 30 July 2024) Art. 5 bans sitting or lying on the ground, or on the steps of churches and other monumental buildings, anywhere in the historic centre, and bans using balustrades, steps and monuments as a rest for things. It also bans lying on benches and climbing the parapets of the city walls and the Medici Fortress. The Art. 5 penalty line was not read; other articles of the regulation carry fines of EUR 50 to EUR 300.
